# CHAPTER
TWENTY-SEVEN
The Siege of Sub-Level 4

Smoke poured through the ventilation grates, carrying the acrid stench of cordite and burning insulation. Lucas led the group through the secondary maintenance corridors, moving in low, synchronized intervals.

Ahead of them, two black-armored corporate security enforcers rounded the corner, their high-tech visor displays glowing an icy predatory blue. Their carbines were already rising to bear.

Lucas didn’t hesitate.

Dropping his center of gravity, he closed the distance with terrifying speed, deflecting the lead operator’s muzzle upward as a burst of suppressed rounds chewed into the concrete ceiling. Using the momentum, Lucas drove an open-palm strike directly into the enforcer's throat guard, followed by a sweeping low kick that swept the man’s legs out from under him. Before the second guard could acquire his target, Sally stepped around the bulkhead and fired from the hip. The heavy shotgun roar shattered the confines of the corridor, blowing the second enforcer backward into the blast door.

“Clean!” Sally grunted, racking another shell into the chamber with a crisp metallic snap.

“Down here!” Lucas pointed to an inconspicuous utility alcove marked with peeling yellow hazard stripes. Behind a tangle of rusted coolant conduits was an emergency maintenance hatch secured by a six-bolt mechanical wheel.

“This leads to the old drainage sumps,” Rolle said skeptically. “It’s a dead end.”

“It was a dead end fifty years ago,” Lucas said, gripping the wheel. He strained against the rusted metal, his muscles burning until the ancient gears reluctantly broke free with a loud screech. “Joe had his engineers cut an emergency bypass directly into the subterranean elevator hoistway.”

The heavy circular hatch swung outward, revealing a vertical drop into absolute blackness. A rusted steel ladder descended into the depths alongside thick bundles of armored power cables.

Above them, the distinct thrum of corporate quad-rotor combat drones buzzed down the hallway, accompanied by the heavy, measured boots of a full tactical assault squad.

“Go! Go! Down the ladder!” Lucas ordered, covering the corridor with his carbine.

Victoria and Emma scrambled into the shaft first, followed by Doc, who grumbled under her breath about her aching knees but moved with surprising agility. Job followed immediately behind her.

“Rolle, plant the charges on the frame!” Lucas called out.

“Already armed, kid!” Rolle slapped two magnetic thermite blocks against the heavy steel hinges of the hatch. “Ten-second delay!”

Sally grabbed Lucas by the collar of his tactical jacket and bodily hauled him into the shaft just as a hail of armor-piercing rounds peppered the entrance. Rolle dropped in behind them, pulling the hatch shut. Two seconds later, the thermite charges ignited in a blinding white glare of three-thousand-degree fury, melting the steel hatch into the mountain rock and fusing the entrance forever.

The team descended through the dark, guided only by the narrow beams of their weapon-mounted lights. Fifty feet down, the ladder terminated on a reinforced concrete catwalk overlooking an immense underground cavern.

Before them stood the primary entrance to the Automated Redoubt Complex.

It was unlike anything Lucas had ever seen. A massive vault door, forty feet in diameter, constructed of solid titanium-tungsten alloy, set flush into the subterranean bedrock. In the center of the door was a sleek biometric terminal, its green standby light blinking patiently in the gloom, powered by geothermal relays that had never stopped running.

Behind them, the distant muffled thuds of corporate shaped charges began hammering through the rock ceiling above. The Directorate forces were drilling through the secondary elevator shafts.

“We’re out of time, Lucas!” Emma shouted over the rumble of collapsing rock above. “They’ll be through the ceiling in two minutes!”

Lucas stepped up to the terminal. The screen flickered to life as his shadow crossed its sensors. An amber prompt appeared on the black glass:
*RESTRICTED FACILITY. CONTINUITY OF GOVERNMENT PROTOCOL ACTIVE. IDENTIFY OR BE TERMINATED.*

Lucas swallowed hard. He placed his right palm against the cold scanner plate.

A lattice of red laser light swept across his skin, reading the ridge patterns, the capillary pulse, and the deep genetic sequence of his blood.

*BIOMETRIC MATCH IDENTIFIED: DESCENDANT PATTERN - WALKER LINEAGE.*
*ENTER SECONDARY CIPHER.*

Lucas leaned in close to the audio receiver. In his mind, he saw Joe standing at the console fifty years ago, looking out into the dark.

“*Adonias has fallen. The Republic endures,*” Lucas spoke clearly.

For three agonizing seconds, nothing happened. The sound of corporate breaching saws roared through the upper catwalks as concrete dust rained down upon their heads.

Then, deep within the mountain, a series of colossal hydraulic locks disengaged with sounds like artillery cannons firing. A blast of pressurized, clean, conditioned air hissed out from the seal, smelling of ozone and pine. The forty-foot titanium vault door slowly recessed two feet into the bedrock and slid silently to the left, revealing the glowing interior of the ARC.

“Get inside! Move!” Lucas commanded.

The team sprinted across the threshold. As Lucas crossed the line, he hit the emergency cycle button on the inner console. The massive door immediately reversed course, sealing shut with a definitive, earth-shaking thud, locking the corporate strike teams out on the cold stone of the cavern.
